To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the dystrophin-deficiency of mdx mice results in sarcolemmal damage; (ii) dystrophin mutations with severe consequences for the sarcolemma are associated with a more severe clinical phenotype in humans; and (iii) laminin α2-deficiency in the dy/dy mouse does not result in a similar degree of sarcolemmal disruption.
the extent of sarcolemmal damage in animal models for Duchenne musculardystrophy correlates with the severity of dystrophin mutations present in humans.
Evans blue dye accumulates in dystrophin-defective muscle but not in laminin α2-defective muscle, indicating that the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex has a different function in muscular dystrophy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathophysiology of muscular dystrophy and with the development of new animal models.
the pathophysiological role of the dystrophins and the DGC in muscular dystrophies.
the pathophysiology of muscular dystrophy, a group of inherited disorders characterized by progressive muscle weakness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sarcolemmal damage in dystrophic muscle fibers, as detected by Evans blue incorporation, is dependent on the type of mutation, the animal model used, and the type of muscle tissue examined.
the DGC is a complex of proteins with a multitude of different functions, and that the pathogenic consequences in muscular dystrophies are not only due to the loss of a single function of the DGC.
the dystrophin-associated protein complex protects the sarcolemmal membrane against contraction-induced injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
different mutations in different components of the dystroglycan complex lead to different pathophysiology in muscular dystrophy.
the DGC is a multifunctional complex with multiple roles in the maintenance of sarcolemmal stability and muscle fiber homeostasis.
the DGC has a protective effect on the sarcolemma in Duchenne muscular Dystrophy but not in Congenital muscular dystrophy.
